about.title: Montebello Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Montebello's mix of warehouses, retail centers, and industrial yards near SR-60 means workplace injuries happen in a lot of different settings — from loading dock falls to equipment accidents. Under California law, workers' compensation is generally your only path against your employer, no matter who was at fault, but that's not always the end of the story. If a subcontractor, property owner, delivery driver, or equipment manufacturer contributed to your injury, a separate third-party claim may be possible alongside your workers' comp benefits. You have 30 days to report the injury to your employer, and retaliation for reporting is against the law. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free connection service that matches injured workers in Montebello with an independent attorney who can look at both the workers' comp side and any third-party angle, at no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your Montebello Workplace Injury

items.title: Workers' Comp Isn't Always the Whole Picture
items.desc: Because workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, injured workers often overlook that a negligent third party — like a subcontractor or equipment maker — could still be liable separately.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter
items.desc: California requires you to report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, and missing that window can complicate your claim, so timing matters from day one.

items.title: Retaliation Protections Exist
items.desc: It's illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury, and an attorney can help you understand those protections if you feel pressured after filing a claim.

items.question: I was hurt while driving for work near Beverly Boulevard — does workers' comp cover that?
items.answer: Generally yes, workplace injuries that happen during job duties, including driving for work, are typically covered by workers' compensation regardless of fault. If another driver caused the crash, though, you may also have a separate third-party claim against that driver. An independent attorney can help sort out how the two claims interact.

items.question: Can I sue my employer directly for my injury?
items.answer: In most cases, no — California workers' compensation is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, even if they were careless. However, if someone other than your employer contributed to the accident, like a contractor or manufacturer, a separate claim against that party may be available.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a third-party claim tied to my Montebello workplace injury?
items.answer: Third-party injury claims in California generally carry a two-year deadline from the date of injury. That's separate from the 30-day window for reporting the injury to your employer for workers' comp purposes, so it helps to understand both timelines early.
